d5_rule: Danger = ANY unpaid past month (not just previous month); Completed overrides Danger when months paid >= tenure; zero-value = unpaid preserved

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: query params tab (holdings | watching), q (search), rating, payout, issuer, status, sort, dir, density, row; bonds rows incl FR-40 fields + watch_state; payment_ledger rows; today's date; live D5 statuses (AF-14); density persisted via query param + alert_prefs
OUTPUT: two-view payload: holdings_count + watching_count (one request, status bar + tabs); filtered row list for the active tab, each row = FR-40 fields + status + next_payout (month, amount, credit_day) + maturity_days + expired flag; visible_count; active filter/sort/density echo; capped flag + true count when > 200 rows; empty list with zero counts when nothing matches
ERRORS: unparseable date field, unknown sort key, or ledger/status query failure -> raise named error ERR-watchlist-query naming the failing stage via AF-30; a failure never renders as a silent empty table (FR-21)
1. Count both tabs first: holdings_count = COUNT(bonds WHERE watch_state='holding'), watching_count = COUNT(... ='watching') — same request, no second query (FR-39 tab labels, FR-49 status bar).
2. Select the tab set: bonds WHERE watch_state matches tab (default 'holdings'); the view split is exact — no row crosses views (FR-39, FR-41).
3. Total before filters: visible_count_total = size of the tab set; apply AND-combined filters from params: rating = exact match on rating value (filter 'AA' returns ONLY rows whose rating is 'AA' — 'AA+'/'AA-' are different chips) (FR-41); payout -> payout_cycle exact; issuer -> issuer_type exact; status -> via the live D5 engine (AF-14) — NOT a stored column.
4. Search (q): case-insensitive substring over company OR ISIN.
5. Per row compute maturity_days = (end_date - today).days; clamp at 0 and set expired = true when <= 0 (matured rows never show negative countdown); NULL end_date -> countdown '—', no crash.
6. Per row compute next_payout: walk the tenure window months in order; the first month with no ledger row, paid flag false, OR amount 0 (zero = unpaid preserved) is next_payout.month; amount = that month's ledger row amount if a row exists, else the payout-cycle scheduled amount (interest_payout apportioned over tenure, same arithmetic as the payout schedule view) when interest_payout is set, else null (rendered '—'); when every due month is paid (or window exhausted / Completed) next_payout = none.
7. SORT WHITELIST: map sort param to a column expression — maturity -> end_date, company -> company, rating -> rating, invested -> amount, next payout -> next_payout.month; any other sort key -> named error naming the key (never a silent default); dir ascending|descending (default ascending); tie-break by company then id for stable order; no sort param -> default order = next payout soonest (FR-41).
8. DENSITY: read density param (compact | comfortable), else the persisted alert_prefs value shared with Settings General; density affects render only — the query does not re-shape rows (FR-41, FR-46).
9. Row cap: apply LIMIT 200 to the returned list; set capped=true and carry the TRUE visible_count above the cap; the template shows the visible note 'showing first 200 rows (offline cap)' — documented cap, no pagination (FR-41).
10. Echo active filter chips (q, rating, payout, issuer, status, sort, dir, density) so removable chips and UI state restore from the same request; the row param (if present) resolves the drawer position id (AF-54).
11. Query-only: no filter/sort/count result is persisted; every render recomputes (DATA-05).
entries.complexity_note: one parameterized scan O(bonds) plus O(bonds x due-window) next-payout walk; bounded offline by the documented LIMIT 200 cap (target < 0.5s at 150x96 per test plan)
edge_cases: watching tab with zero rows -> empty list, visible_count 0, watching_count 0 (legitimate empty, not an error); holdings_count still true
position with every due month paid -> next_payout none; matured position -> maturity_days 0 with expired flag; NULL end_date -> '—'
amount 0 ledger row in the current month -> counts unpaid (zero = unpaid preserved), becomes next_payout
sort=foo (not in the whitelist) -> named error naming the unknown key, no silent default sort
rating filter 'AA' with rows 'AA+' and 'AA' -> only the exact 'AA' row returns
300 matching rows -> 200 returned, capped=true, visible_count 300, offline-cap note rendered
Completed position in holdings tab -> still listed; status filter 'Completed' selects it via live D5 engine

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: AF-52 row set for the active tab (same request); payment_ledger rows for those positions; today's date
OUTPUT: four tile payloads: total_investment, current_returns, next_payout_this_month (+due_count), maturing_90_days (+bond_count); sub-line counts (visible rows of total positions)
ERRORS: row-set or ledger aggregate failure -> raise named error ERR-watchlist-summary naming the tile via AF-30; never render zeroed tiles over a failed table (FR-21)
1. Receive the SAME AF-52 row set that the table renders — tiles and rows share one query pass (no independent re-query that could disagree with the table).
2. Tile 1 Total Invested = SUM(row.amount) over the tab's rows; sub-line = '{visible_count} visible rows of {view_total} positions'.
3. Tile 2 Current Returns = SUM(payment_ledger.amount) over those bond ids WHERE paid = 1 AND amount > 0 (zero = unpaid preserved).
4. Tile 3 Next Payout This Month: select rows whose next_payout.month == current month key; value = SUM of their next_payout amounts (null amounts contribute 0 but keep the row in due_count); due_count = their row count (mockup shape '₹7,500.00 / 3 due').
5. Tile 4 Maturing in 90 Days: count rows where 0 <= maturity_days <= 90; expired rows (maturity_days 0 AND expired flag) are matured, not maturing, and are excluded; sub-line = '{n} bonds'.
6. Return the four payloads; the template renders values with the shared INR money formatter (privacy mask applies per AF-43 at render).
entries.complexity_note: four O(rows) aggregates over the AF-52 row set in a single pass
edge_cases: empty tab -> all four tiles zero / counts 0, table empty — consistent, not an error
position maturing in exactly 90 days -> included; day 91 -> excluded; matured (expired) -> excluded
current month with three unpaid rows at ₹7,500.00 total -> tile ₹7,500.00 with due_count 3 matching the three rows
ledger row with amount 0 -> excluded from Current Returns (zero = unpaid)
a due row whose next_payout amount is null -> counted in due_count, contributes 0 to the sum (no fabricated figure)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: position id (GET /watch/<id> fragment, fallback /watch?row=<id>); bonds row for the id (FR-40 fields, dates, watch_state, credit_day); payment_ledger rows for the id; live D5 status (AF-14); tab context (holdings | watching)
OUTPUT: drawer fragment/payload {facts: {isin, face_value, secured, issuer_type, rating, rating_agency, start_date, end_date, credit_day, payout_cycle, company}, yield_box: {invested, returned, coupon_pct, expected_yield_pct}, schedule: [{month, state: received | overdue | upcoming}], actions: [...], manual_rating_note}; named not-found error for unknown id
ERRORS: unknown position id, unparseable dates, tenure < 1, or ledger/status failure -> raise named error ERR-drawer-payload naming the id via AF-30; never open a drawer with an empty or fabricated payload (FR-21)
1. Resolve the row: GET /watch/<id> (or row param) -> SELECT bonds WHERE id = ? ; row absent -> raise named not-found error naming the id.
2. Build facts grid: ISIN, face_value, secured, issuer_type, rating + rating_agency, start/end date, credit_day + payout_cycle, company; status from the live D5 engine (AF-14).
3. Build yield box: invested (amount), returned (paid ledger sum), coupon_pct, expected_yield_pct + the offline 'ratings entered manually' note (honesty: no market feed, D33).
4. Build the tenure window months from start_date + tenure_months (same arithmetic as the status engine); classify each month: received = ledger row with paid flag true AND amount > 0; overdue = in window, unpaid (zero = unpaid preserved), AND past (month < current, OR month == current AND today.day > credit_day); upcoming = otherwise. schedule = classified list in month order (FR-42).
5. actions: base = [Edit, Record Payment]; if watch_state == 'watching' add Move to Holdings (AF-55); if 'holding' add Mark as Watching — actions emitted per tab so the wrong-direction action never renders (FR-39, FR-42).
6. Money fields pass through the privacy mask helper at render time (AF-43) before display; the fragment is returned for client-side open (no page reload), server-rendered fallback keeps the drawer open with no JavaScript state (/watch?row=<id>).
entries.complexity_note: one row read plus one ledger read and an O(tenure) window classification
edge_cases: id not found -> named not-found error, drawer does not open
position with unparseable start_date -> named error naming the field, not a crash
ledger row amount 0 in an elapsed month -> schedule shows 'overdue' (zero = unpaid), status engine agrees
current month unpaid but today <= credit_day -> 'upcoming' (due window not passed); day after credit_day while unpaid -> 'overdue'
watching row's drawer -> actions include Move to Holdings, exclude Mark as Watching (and vice versa)
Completed position -> drawer opens fully; schedule shows all months received where paid

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: position id to move (POST /watch/<id>/move); its bonds row (company, isin, watch_state, amount, start_date, end_date, credit_day); bonds table scan for active positions with live D5 statuses (AF-14 via AF-39)
OUTPUT: watch_state updated 'watching' -> 'holding' on pass; blocked verdict with named error ERR-move-watching (zero writes) on missing mandatory field or lock conflict; named state errors for unknown id / already-holding row
ERRORS: missing/invalid mandatory holding field OR active-position lock conflict -> ERR-move-watching naming the field or the blocking position + status; unknown id or already 'holding' -> named state error; none of these write anything (FR-21, FR-39)
1. Resolve the row by id; absent -> named not-found error, no write.
2. If watch_state == 'holding' -> named error 'already in Holdings', no write (idempotence is explicit, not silent).
3. MANDATORY HOLDING FIELDS (checked FIRST — a candidate may lack them): amount present and numeric >= 0; start_date and end_date parseable dates with end_date after start_date; credit_day an integer in 1..28. Any violation -> raise ERR-move-watching naming the missing/invalid field (e.g. 'Cannot move: credit_day missing') and write nothing — a candidate with holes can never become a holding.
4. D15 LOCK RE-CHECK (the highlight — moving INTO holdings re-runs the active-position lock, it is not add-time-only): run the AF-39 scan with the moving row's keys: company_key = company.trim().lower(), isin_key = isin.trim().upper(); scan ALL OTHER bonds rows; skip rows whose live D5 status == 'Completed'; for each remaining row compute stored_company / stored_isin normalized the same way; name_match = (company_key non-empty AND stored_company == company_key); isin_match = (isin_key non-empty AND stored_isin == isin_key); if name_match OR isin_match -> HARD BLOCK: raise ERR-move-watching 'Cannot move: {stored_company} has an active position ({status})' naming the blocking position — no override, no force-accept, zero rows updated (D15 applied exactly: EITHER key matches -> blocked; lock releases only at Completed).
5. Lock pass (no active match) -> UPDATE bonds SET watch_state = 'holding' WHERE id = ? ; rowcount must be exactly 1, else raise the named state error (0 = raced/deleted, >1 = impossible under PK but guarded).
6. Only watch_state changes: status, ledger rows and FR-40 fields are untouched — the move alters view membership, not position history.
7. Surface the outcome visibly via AF-30: success = confirmation naming the position; block = the ERR-move-watching banner naming the blocking position or field — never redirect a block as success (FR-21).
entries.complexity_note: one O(bonds) normalized scan (same cost as the add-time lock) plus one single-row UPDATE; field validation is constant-time
edge_cases: watching 'Alpha' (ISIN X123) moved while active holding 'Alpha' (On-going) exists -> blocked by name match, ERR-move-watching
watching row whose company matches only a Completed position -> passes (Completed excluded from the active set)
ISIN collision with different company name -> still blocked (EITHER key matches)
candidate row with NULL credit_day or missing amount -> blocked at mandatory-fields step, ERR-move-watching naming the field, lock never runs
row already 'holding' -> named state error, no duplicate effect
two watch rows of the same company moved one after the other -> first move passes, second blocks against the now-active first (lock re-checked every move)
move blocked -> tab counts and table unchanged; no partial write

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: credit-day sweep results / Danger flags (AF-46); notifications rows from the AF-47 cadence (before_due, day_of, overdue); bonds end_date vs today with maturity_30/7/1 toggles and reminder_days from alert_prefs; alert_prefs unique-key dedupe registry; dismissal state (panel only)
OUTPUT: merged card list {card_type: overdue | due_soon | maturity_soon, bond_id, company, message, severity, dedupe_key, created_at} sorted severity-first then timestamp desc; alerts-today count for the status bar; bell badge unread contribution; dedupe registry rows
ERRORS: scan/insert/query failure -> raise named error ERR-notify-build naming the source scan and position via AF-30; a position is never silently skipped (ERR-01, FR-21)
1. OVERDUE cards (red): for each position where today.day > credit_day AND current month unpaid (no row, flag false, OR amount 0 — zero = unpaid preserved; the day-wise engine has flagged it Danger): dedupe_key = 'danger:{bond_id}:{YYYY-MM-DD}'; insert-or-ignore into the dedupe registry; suppressed key -> no card (re-running the sweep the same day is idempotent).
2. DUE-SOON cards (amber): current-cycle month unpaid AND (lead window: credit_day - reminder_days <= today.day < credit_day, with reminder_days from alert_prefs default 2) -> dedupe_key = 'due:{bond_id}:{YYYY-MM}'; OR day-of (today.day == credit_day, unpaid) -> dedupe_key = 'dayof:{bond_id}:{YYYY-MM}'; insert-or-ignore suppression on both — the same (position, month) never stacks two due cards.
3. MATURITY cards (accent): days_left = (end_date - today).days; fire only when days_left is EXACTLY 30, 7 or 1 AND that horizon's toggle (maturity_30 / maturity_7 / maturity_1) is enabled in alert_prefs: dedupe_key = 'maturity:{bond_id}:{days_left}'; suppress on repeat (each horizon fires once per position); message names the company, the end date and the days remaining.
4. Merge: concatenate the three card lists; sort key = (severity rank overdue > due_soon > maturity_soon, created_at desc, bond_id); each card keeps its dedupe_key for auditability.
5. DISMISSAL IS PANEL STATE ONLY (the highlight): dismissing a card removes it from the panel view ONLY — never DELETE the notifications history row (original timestamp retained) and never DELETE the alert_prefs dedupe marker; the same event cannot re-fire into a new history row after dismissal (FR-43, FR-34).
6. Bell badge = count of unread feed contributions; alerts-today count feeds the shell status bar from the same watchlist request (FR-49).
7. Email for the same events remains AF-48's job; no SMS/WhatsApp/push channel exists (D24 deferred).
entries.complexity_note: three O(bonds) scan passes plus one insert-or-ignore per firing key; one ordered list build
edge_cases: daily sweep runs twice same day -> danger/due/dayof keys already registered, second run adds zero cards
credit day missed today -> overdue card the same day (danger: key for today) + bell badge increments (SRS FR-43 AC)
maturity_7 toggle off with exactly 7 days left -> no card; toggle on and 7 days left -> card with maturity:{id}:7
app closed on the exact 30/7/1-day mark (missed) -> that horizon's key never registered but the day passed -> no card that horizon (exact-day windows only — documented offline behavior)
dismiss overdue card -> panel clears it, notifications history row with same timestamp remains, dedupe key remains
position Completed -> no cadence or overdue cards fire (no payment due); maturity card still allowed until end_date
alert_prefs missing maturity toggles -> treated as enabled defaults per AF-57 defaults (maturity 30/7/1 on)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: alert_prefs settings keys [smtp_host, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_app_password, alert_to, alert_from_name, reminder_days, overdue_on, maturity_30, maturity_7, maturity_1, sweep_time, default_credit_day, privacy_default, csv_scope] + density (shared watchlist/General); runtime keys (last_sweep, notify_once markers) skipped; environment vars SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_APP_PASSWORD, ALERT_TO; built-in defaults
OUTPUT: per-key view {stored_value, effective_value, source: env | stored | default}; smtp_configured boolean; smtp_app_password as masked marker only; missing-key report for first-run display
ERRORS: malformed stored value (non-integer smtp_port, port outside 1..65535, invalid csv_scope enum, credit day outside 1..28, sweep hour outside 0..23) -> raise named error ERR-settings-load naming the key via AF-30; never silently substitute a default over a malformed value (FR-21)
1. Load alert_prefs rows into a stored map (key -> value); an empty table is a legitimate first-run state. Filter OUT runtime keys (last_sweep, notify_once dedupe markers) — they are never returned (FR-44, FR-45).
2. PRECEDENCE MATRIX (the highlight — resolve EACH key top-down, first non-empty wins):
   2a. ENV LAYER (highest), for exactly five keys: SMTP_HOST -> smtp_host; SMTP_PORT -> smtp_port; SMTP_USER -> smtp_user; SMTP_APP_PASSWORD -> smtp_app_password; ALERT_TO -> alert_to. Non-empty env value WINS over stored; provenance = 'env'.
   2b. STORED LAYER (middle): key present in alert_prefs with non-empty value -> wins over default; provenance = 'stored'.
   2c. DEFAULT LAYER (lowest): smtp_host = 'smtp.gmail.com', smtp_port = 465 (SSL), csv_scope = 'current_view', reminder_days = 2, overdue_on = 1, maturity_30/7/1 = 1, privacy_default = 0; theme has NO key (fixed dark) and INR format is a fixed radio (no key); provenance = 'default'.
   2d. NEVER invert: stored never overrides env; default never overrides stored; env is never written back to storage (the matrix is env > stored > default for the five shared keys, stored > default for all others).
3. Validate RESOLVED values: smtp_port int in 1..65535; default_credit_day int 1..28; reminder_days >= 0 int; sweep_time int 0..23; csv_scope in {current_view, full_ledger}; density in {compact, comfortable} — malformed RESOLVED value raises the named error naming key + value.
4. Return per key BOTH stored_value (Settings form binds this, annotated 'overridden by environment' when source='env' so a stale stored username is never shown without the env-wins note) AND effective_value (send path + indicators use this) AND source.
5. SECRET MASKING: smtp_app_password output = masked marker ('••••') when any layer resolved a value, else 'unset' — the clear value never leaves this function (never returned, never logged).
6. smtp_configured = smtp_user AND smtp_app_password AND alert_to all resolvable (stored or their env overrides; host/port have built-in defaults); the status bar renders 'Email: not configured' (muted/red) until all three exist and shows configured/not only — never a value, never a username (FR-44, FR-49).
entries.complexity_note: one table read plus a constant-time per-key three-layer merge; O(keys)
edge_cases: env SMTP_USER set, stored smtp_user different -> effective_value from env (source 'env'), stored_value still shown in the form with the env-wins annotation
no env vars at all -> stored values used; keys absent from storage -> defaults, source 'default'
stored smtp_port 'abc' -> named ERR-settings-load naming smtp_port, no silent default
stored smtp_app_password present -> output masked marker, smtp_configured per three-key rule, clear value never emitted
empty alert_prefs (first run) -> all defaults, smtp_configured false unless env supplies the three keys, missing-key report lists every key
ALERT_TO unset everywhere -> falls back to smtp_user as recipient (mailer's existing default) and configured flag reflects the fallback
runtime key last_sweep present in alert_prefs -> filtered out, never shown in any Settings section

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: POST body scoped to one section (email | alerts | general | data); current alert_prefs rows (for write-once merge); existing stored smtp_app_password
OUTPUT: upserted alert_prefs rows for exactly that section's keys; password write-once outcome (kept | replaced); success confirmation or named per-key validation error (ERR-settings-save)
ERRORS: invalid smtp_port / default_credit_day / reminder_days / sweep_time / csv_scope / density / theme / boolean toggle -> named error ERR-settings-save naming the key via AF-30, NOTHING written for that section (FR-21)
1. Determine the section from the route; build its key set: email -> [smtp_host, smtp_port, smtp_user, smtp_app_password, alert_to, alert_from_name]; alerts -> [reminder_days, overdue_on, maturity_30, maturity_7, maturity_1, sweep_time]; general -> [default_credit_day, privacy_default, density] (INR format fixed radio and theme fixed dark carry NO keys — theme accepts only 'dark', Light disabled as coming later); data -> [csv_scope]. Other sections' keys are NEVER touched — a partial form cannot blank unrelated settings (FR-44, FR-45, FR-46, FR-47).
2. WRITE-ONCE PASSWORD (the highlight): if the body's smtp_app_password field is ABSENT, blank or whitespace-only -> SKIP the key entirely: the stored value is kept, not cleared, not overwritten (blank KEEPS old); if non-blank -> validate non-empty after trim and replace the stored value. In BOTH cases the stored secret is never echoed into the response or the re-rendered form (FR-44).
3. VALIDATE every present key before any write: smtp_port parses as int AND 1..65535; default_credit_day int AND 1..28; reminder_days non-negative int; sweep_time int 0..23 (daily sweep hour); density in {compact, comfortable}; csv_scope in {current_view, full_ledger} (UI labels Current view / Full ledger); toggles (overdue_on, maturity_30, maturity_7, maturity_1, privacy_default) accept 0/1 only; theme accepts 'dark' only. Any violation -> named error naming the key + offending value; abort this section's write (fail the whole section, no partial half-validated state).
4. UPSERT per validated key: INSERT INTO alert_prefs (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value — saving twice converges to one row per key; the unique-key invariant holds (FR-44).
5. WRITE ONLY the submitted section's key set (step 1); commit once per section save.
6. Shared density: saving density in General updates the same persisted key the watchlist density switch writes/reads — one setting, two controls; the next watchlist render picks it up immediately (FR-46).
7. Reload via AF-57 after commit and return the view for the UI; env-layer values are untouched — save never writes to the environment, and env still overrides the newly stored value at read/send time (FR-44 precedence preserved).
entries.complexity_note: per-section O(keys) validation plus one upsert per key; single transaction per section
edge_cases: email section saved with blank password field -> other email keys updated, stored password unchanged (write-once), no secret in response
password field non-blank -> stored replaced; subsequent AF-57 load returns only the masked marker
smtp_port 70000 or 'abc' -> ERR-settings-save naming smtp_port, section not written, UI shows pre-save values
sweep_time posted as 24 or 'on' -> named validation error naming the key (hour must be 0..23)
general section save does not touch smtp_* keys (section scoping); data save only touches csv_scope
same key saved twice -> single alert_prefs row per key (upsert), no duplicates
user edits smtp_user while env SMTP_USER is set -> stored value saved but AF-57 effective value stays env (form shows env-wins annotation)

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: effective SMTP config from AF-57 (env > stored > default merge): host, port, user, app password, recipient; synthetic event dict {company: 'Test Alert', month: today's YYYY-MM, severity: 'test', credit_day: n/a}; mailer send path (AF-48 / mailer.send_alert_email unchanged)
OUTPUT: one sent test email (subject 'test: Test Alert payment YYYY-MM') + visible inline success banner (recipient, subject); OR visible named-error inline banner ERR-smtp-unconfigured / ERR-test-email with the page rendering normally (HTTP 500 page never); no production notification row
ERRORS: missing config after merge -> ERR-smtp-unconfigured naming the missing item BEFORE any connection; auth/connection/send failure -> ERR-test-email with the underlying reason; a test failure is never an HTTP 500 and never a silent no-op (FR-21, FR-44)
1. Resolve config via AF-57's merge: env SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_USER/SMTP_APP_PASSWORD/ALERT_TO override stored alert_prefs values for this send (FR-44 precedence).
2. CONFIG GATE before any connection: smtp_user and smtp_app_password must both resolve (recipient falls back to user per mailer default); missing -> raise/surface ERR-smtp-unconfigured naming the missing item (e.g. 'SMTP_APP_PASSWORD is not set') — no default credential, no silent skip, no send attempt (FR-44).
3. Build the synthetic event dict: company 'Test Alert', month = today's month key, severity 'test', credit_day n/a. It is SYNTHETIC: never written to notifications history and never registered in the dedupe registry (FR-43 integrity).
4. Delegate to mailer.send_alert_email unchanged — NO second mail path: connect host:port (SSL on 465, STARTTLS on 587 or SMTP_STARTTLS=1), login with user + app password, sendmail From user To recipient, subject '<severity>: <company> payment <month>'.
5. SUCCESS -> visible inline confirmation banner naming the actual recipient and subject; configured/not indicator unchanged (a test mutates no settings, no history rows).
6. FAILURE -> catch transport/auth exception; surface ERR-test-email in an INLINE banner with the underlying reason (wrong password -> authentication failed; network down -> connection refused); the Settings page renders with the banner — no HTTP 500 page, no swallowed exception, no fake success (FR-44, FR-21).
7. The App Password is passed only from the resolved config — never hardcoded, never logged, never echoed in the response body.
entries.complexity_note: one config merge plus one SMTP session; single synchronous send per click
edge_cases: no config anywhere (fresh install) -> ERR-smtp-unconfigured banner at step 2, zero connections attempted
env SMTP_APP_PASSWORD set, stored blank -> env wins, send proceeds with env credential
wrong app password -> SMTP auth error captured -> ERR-test-email inline banner, Settings page intact (no 500)
network down -> connection failure -> ERR-test-email banner; no notification/history row left behind
ALERT_TO unset -> recipient falls back to resolved smtp_user (personal-to-personal), success banner names that recipient
double-click Test Email -> two independent sends; neither writes dedupe keys, so no interference with AF-56

entries.pseudocode:
INPUT: POST backup (no parameters); POST reset carrying confirm_word; live database file path (DB_PATH); schema initialization routine (AF-01 normal init path / SCHEMA_STATEMENTS)
OUTPUT: backup -> downloadable .db file stream saved to the user's chosen location; reset on pass -> backup artifact taken BEFORE wipe, then empty re-initialized schema (all six tables present and empty); failure -> named error with zero deletion
ERRORS: confirm_word != 'RESET' -> ERR-reset-db, zero deletion; backup read failure -> named backup error, reset ABORTS (no wipe without a recoverable copy); re-init failure -> named error via AF-30 (FR-21)
1. BACKUP PATH (standalone Export backup (.db)): open the DB file read-only; stream its bytes as a downloadable .db file to the user's chosen location; a missing/unreadable file or zero-byte read raises the named backup error — never offered as a valid backup (FR-47).
2. RESET PATH step 1 — RESET CONFIRM (the highlight): server-side comparison confirm_word == literal 'RESET' EXACTLY (case-sensitive); 'reset', 'Reset', ' RESET ' with padding, or empty -> raise ERR-reset-db 'Reset requires typed confirmation RESET' and DELETE NOTHING. The browser confirm dialog alone is NEVER sufficient — the check is enforced server-side in the POST handler (FR-47).
3. RESET PATH step 2 — BACKUP-BEFORE-WIPE (the highlight): when the confirmation matches, take the backup first (step 1 machinery) and verify the artifact is non-empty; if backup fails -> ABORT the reset with a named error, database left fully intact — no wipe ever runs without a recoverable copy (FR-47).
4. RESET PATH step 3 — WIPE: delete the database file (or clear it atomically per implementation); from this point on the only acceptable end state is a re-initialized schema.
5. RESET PATH step 4 — RE-INIT through the normal init path: run AF-01 initialization (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for bonds, payment_ledger, financial_goals, notifications, alert_prefs, share_config + column backfill); verify every table exists afterward; empty alert_prefs restores defaults-on-read via AF-57 (FR-47).
6. All-or-nothing: failure at step 2/3 leaves the ORIGINAL database (nothing wiped); failure at step 5 surfaces a named error naming the step — the app never proceeds against a half-dropped file (FR-21).
7. Success -> visible confirmation (backup retained + reset complete); the next render shows zero positions/notifications — structural validity guaranteed by step 5's table-existence check.
entries.complexity_note: one full-file copy for backup; reset is wipe + O(tables) schema creation — constant structure, data-dependent size
edge_cases: confirm word 'reset' lowercase or 'Reset' capital-R or 'RESET ' with trailing space -> rejected (exact case-sensitive literal match), nothing deleted (SRS FR-47 AC)
confirm correct but backup read fails -> reset aborts, original DB untouched and app still runs
backup succeeds, wipe succeeds, re-init fails -> named error surfaced; never a silent partial schema
reset on a brand-new empty DB -> still runs backup + full re-init; converges to empty schema
concurrent query during reset -> connection sees either full original or empty re-initialized DB, never mid-wipe state (single-path handler)
post-reset alert_prefs empty -> AF-57 returns all defaults; environment variables still override (unchanged precedence)
